title: Descent of finite relations among module maps
statement: Let I be a directed set and let (S_i)_{i\in I} be an inverse system of quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms, where S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R_i) for Noetherian rings R_i, and let S=\varprojlim_i S_i=\operatorname{Spec}(R). Let X_i be a finitely presented S_i-scheme [def-pc-scheme], put X=X_i\times_{S_i}S and X_j=X_i\times_{S_i}S_j for j\ge i [def-pc-base-change]. Fix a finite collection of finitely presented quasi-coherent \mathcal{O}_X-modules and maps between them, together with finitely presented models of those modules and maps on X_j whose base changes are identified with the given collection. If finitely many specified equalities between composites of the maps hold after base change to X, then, after replacing j by a later stage, all the specified equalities already hold on X_j.

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR (finite relations among descended module maps)

proof.text: The supplied models and maps already are maps between fixed modules on X_j, so no object or map descent is needed. For each specified relation form delta_k=lhs_k-rhs_k. Tensor pullback is additive by its adjunction to additive pushforward and Mathlib Adjunction.left_adjoint_additive. The hypothesis makes its pullback zero. Finite presentation of the source implies finite type. Apply [lem-pc-fp-zero-map-descent] to obtain a stage where this one difference is zero. Additivity and sub_eq_zero recover equality of the two maps there.

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR (3), first proof; Algebra Tag 05N7 (3), finite-generator vanishing argument

proof.text: Apply Finset.exists_le to j together with the finite image of all the chosen stages; the empty collection is included. Compose each individual stage transition with the transition to the common upper bound. Tensor-pullback composition gives a natural isomorphism between direct and successive pullback. Its naturality and cancellation identify the two pulled-back maps, so the equality at the individual stage persists at the common upper bound. Spec.map_comp and R.map_comp identify the composite transition with the transition stated in the conclusion.

theorem finiteRelation_module_map_descent
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u})
    (c : Cone (R.op ⋙ Scheme.Spec)) (hc : IsLimit c) [IsAffine c.pt]
    (i : I) {Xi : Scheme.{u}} (f : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j)
    (M : Type u) [Finite M]
    (Fj : M → (pullback f (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij)))).Modules)
    (hFj_fp : ∀ k : M, (Fj k).IsFinitePresentation)
    (hFj_qc : ∀ k : M, (Fj k).IsQuasicoherent)
    (n : ℕ) (src tgt : Fin n → M)
    (lhs rhs : ∀ k : Fin n, Fj (src k) ⟶ Fj (tgt k))
    (hrel : ∀ k : Fin n,
      (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f
        (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
        (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
        (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op j)) (c.w (homOfLE hij).op))).map (lhs k) =
      (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f
        (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
        (T' := Over.mk (c.π.app (op i)))
        (Over.homMk (c.π.app (op j)) (c.w (homOfLE hij).op))).map (rhs k)) :
    ∃ (j' : I) (hjj' : j ≤ j'),
      ∀ k : Fin n,
        (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f
          (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
          (T' := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE (hij.trans hjj')))))
          (Over.homMk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hjj')))
            (by dsimp; rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← R.map_comp]; rfl))).map (lhs k) =
        (Scheme.Modules.moduleBaseChange f
          (T := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij))))
          (T' := Over.mk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE (hij.trans hjj')))))
          (Over.homMk (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hjj')))
            (by dsimp; rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← R.map_comp]; rfl))).map (rhs k)
